Worca CC · design mockup

Skinning the last of the browser

Thirteen checkbox sites, one radio group, eight blocking system dialogs and a handful of UA widgets still render in the operating system's voice instead of Worca's. This page proposes the whole set, side by side with what ships today.

The mark already exists. .qopt (style.css:761) draws a 1.5px --radio-ring hairline on --panel that fills --green behind a white tick. Every control below inherits that one mark, so "chosen" looks identical whether it is a question option, a checkbox, a chip or a whole row.

01 Checkbox

An 18px rounded square, --radio-ring hairline on --panel, filling --green with the same white tick .qopt.sel uses. Styled on the real <input> via appearance:none — so the rule reaches all thirteen existing sites with no markup change, and for eight of them that is the whole job. With :checked, :disabled, :indeterminate, label-clicks and keyboard all still free.

03 Switch

Worca already has a switch (.switch, style.css:470) — but it is a <div role="switch"> hand-mirrored to a hidden input in JS (app.js:5007). Adding one sibling selector lets the same pixels be driven by a real checkbox, so a new switch costs zero JavaScript and stays accessible for free.

The control

Existing size, plus a .switch-sm for dense rows like a plugin card header.

When it is a switch, when it is a checkbox

The single rule that decides all thirteen sites.
SwitchActs on a live system the moment you flip it. Plugin enabled, chat channel on, notify-on events, mock mode, auto-scroll.
CheckboxPart of a form you then Save or Next. Supported efforts, models to export, projects to scan, fan-out and questions flags, "No cap", the purge opt-in inside a confirm.
Under this rule four sites become switches (plugins-view.mjs:63, chat-settings-view.mjs:36,58) and the other nine keep the box.

04 Selectable rows & chips

When a choice carries more than a word — a name plus a badge, a path, a model id — the box alone cannot show selection at a glance. .opt-row lifts .qopt out of the question panel and makes the whole row the target; the existing .chip-select pill finally gets a checked state.

06 Select

The closed state is already ours (appearance:none + .select-wrap::after). The open popup belongs to the OS and cannot be styled — the only fix is to stop using <select>. Recommendation: keep it for the ten plain-text lists. The OS popup is faster, keyboard-complete, screen-reader-correct and far better on a phone; replacing it buys paint and costs behaviour. Reach for .listbox only where an option needs more than a word.

Keep · plain lists Project, workspace, workflow, branch, guardrails, the four log filters, budget period.
Unchanged. The popup is native and that is the right trade.
Promote · rich options Agent colour (needs a swatch) and the model picker (needs the id under the label) — the two that today flatten real information into one line.
Same .opt-row as §4 — no new component.

07 Dialogs

confirmModal() already exists and eleven callers use it — but eight sites still call window.confirm / window.prompt, including all four destructive deletes. A system alert can't show the app's red, wraps a long warning into an OS paragraph, blocks the event loop, and on Chrome offers "prevent this page from creating more dialogs" — which silently breaks the next one. Two changes finish the job: migrate the eight, and add promptModal() so the two double-prompts become one dialog. The buttons below are live.

Destructive confirm

app.js:2604, 6245, 6663, 8020 — currently window.confirm. danger:true and the red OK button already exist (style.css:1869); nobody is passing them.
The worktree one is the clearest win: three paragraphs of consequence (app.js:9932) currently rendered as an OS alert.

promptModal() — new

Same .confirm-modal shell, plus .confirm-field. Takes an array of fields, so app.js:2464+2467 and app.js:8007+8009 — two blocking prompts back to back — collapse into one dialog with live validation.
